1.g: Pronunciation: the 5 pure vowels, r vs rr, stress rules. Articles and gender.
1.ms: You can read any Spanish word aloud correctly and follow Superbeginner videos using the visuals.

2.g: Present tense of -ar/-er/-ir verbs. Irregulars tener, ir, hacer. ir a + infinitive.
2.ms: You can build simple present-tense sentences and pick out familiar words in slow speech.

3.g: Numbers, dates and telling time. Possessives. gustar and verbs like it.
3.ms: You can say what you like, what day and time it is, and who is in your family.

4.g: Reflexive verbs and daily routine. Stem-changers (e→ie, o→ue, e→i).
4.ms: Beginner videos feel mostly clear; you can describe your daily routine.

5.g: Adjective agreement. ser vs estar in depth. Comparisons (más/menos… que, tan… como).
5.ms: Language Transfer finished. You can describe people, places and feelings.

6.g: Question words. Prepositions of place. por vs para (intro).
6.ms: You can ask for and give basic information and directions.

7.ms: You can talk about finished actions in the past.

8.g: Preterite irregulars: ser/ir, tener, estar, hacer, poder, decir, poner, venir.
8.ms: You can tell a short past-tense story without stopping every sentence.

9.ms: You can describe what things were like and what happened, and choose the right past tense most of the time.

10.g: Direct and indirect object pronouns (lo, la, le, se lo). Informal commands.
10.ms: Pronouns stop tripping you up in listening; you can give instructions.

11.g: Present perfect. Future simple vs ir a.
11.ms: You can talk about experiences and future plans.

12.g: Conditional. Review of all tenses so far.
12.ms: All core indicative tenses in place. Intermediate content is comfortable with occasional pauses.

13.ms: You recognise the subjunctive when you hear it.

14.g: Subjunctive after wishes, requests and emotions (quiero que, me alegra que).
14.ms: You can express wishes and feelings about others' actions.

15.g: Subjunctive after doubt, denial and impersonal expressions (es posible que).
15.ms: You've had your first real conversations with native speakers.

16.g: por vs para in depth. se constructions (impersonal and accidental: se me olvidó).
16.ms: Podcasts for learners are understandable without transcripts.

17.ms: You can follow a TV plot with Spanish subtitles.

18.ms: You can talk about hypotheticals. Checkpoint: roughly the end of DS Level 3.

19.ms: Native YouTube in your interest area is mostly understandable.

20.g: Relative pronouns: que, quien, lo que, el cual, cuyo.
20.ms: Your sentences get longer and more connected.

21.g: Regional variation: vosotros, voseo, Spain vs Latin America vocabulary.
21.ms: You can adjust to different accents.

22.g: Subjunctive in adverbial clauses (cuando, para que, aunque, antes de que).
22.ms: You catch most of a native TV episode without subtitles.

23.ms: You can read news and write a structured paragraph.

24.ms: Casual native speech is followable in context.
